en: Puṣkara said: By offering oblations to the Gaṇa Śāntātīta, a human being attains peace;
and by offering oblations to the Gaṇa Bhaiṣajya, one dispels all diseases.
Having offered oblations to this group of twenty-one, one is liberated from all sins;
having offered oblations to the "Fearless" group, one never encounters fear anywhere.
O Rāma, by offering the Aparājita-gaṇa, one is not defeated;
and by offering the Āyuṣya-gaṇa, one wards off untimely death.
By offering the oblation to the Gaṇa Svastyayana, one attains well-being everywhere;
likewise, one attains union with excellence and the host that is armor against harm.
By offering oblations to the host of Vāstoṣpati, one removes the defects of the dwelling;
likewise, by offering oblations to the host of Raudra, one removes all defects.
Indeed, with these ten groups of materials, the fire-oblation is performed during the eighteen pacificatory rites.
The peace of Viṣṇu, that of Indra, and likewise that of Brahmā and Rudra;
as well as that of Vāyu, Varuṇa, Kubera, and Bhṛgu.
Likewise, [the mudrās] belonging to Prajāpati, Tvaṣṭṛ, Kumāra, and the deity Agni;
those of the Marut host, the Gandharvas, and likewise the Nairṛtas, are characterized by tranquility.
O best of the Bhrigus, the pacification rites of Aṅgiras, Yama, and the Earth—
these pacifications are declared to be always beneficial for all ritual acts.
Indeed, this mantra "yas tvā mṛtyuḥ," when recited, is the destroyer of death;
and by offering oblations while reciting the names of one's mother, one shall thus obtain all desires.
And having offered with the mantra "suparṇas tvā," one is not at all harmed by serpents.
And one who desires land should always recite: "yasyedaṃ bhūmyām. (Vdho 2.127.10)
The offering with the mantra "On earth you are the highest" always bestows preeminence;
likewise, that with "He who [is] made of udumbara wood" increases one's vigor.
The mantra "Given by Indra" destroys all afflictions,
and the bath with the mantra "Hiraṇyavarṇā" shall be a remover of sin.
"O best of the Bhrigus, a wise person should employ all the poison-destroying [mantras] beginning with 'Asitasya' and the poison-destroying mantra portions beginning with 'Sarasvatī'."
All [mantras] beginning with Śarabha, as well as those that destroy the Piśācas,
and this mantra "Imā Devī"— this is the supreme performer of all pacification.
"O gods, O Maruts"—this [mantra] fulfills all desires;
"From the world of Yama"—this is the supreme pacifier of bad dreams.
Furthermore, this [mantra] beginning with "agner vaḥ" is said to be the destroyer of anger;
it should be understood as being performed standing upright, having assumed the supreme posture.
"Indra, we [choose] the merchant"— this is supreme for gaining profit from trade;
"Desire is mine, O King"— this increases the good fortune of women.
One should recite "Bhadrāya karṇam" when there is a discharge from the ears;
likewise, "Bhadrāsy akṣirodhe jātā" is for a discharge from the ears.
The oblation "tubhyam eva jariman" bestows longevity;
the oblation "āyātu mitra" brings about the acquisition of friends.
O best of men, one who desires this should perform a fire-oblation with mixed grains; he shall attain lordship everywhere.
"O Agni, [be] with cows"—this is the supreme mantra for increasing cattle;
one should offer oblations for twelve days, especially according to the *parāka* rite.
"The fire is extinguished"—this [utterance] brings well-being to the village;
therefore, by fashioning a mound of earth from the village, one attains equality with the sacrificial altar.
"We know all his intentions regarding the acquisition of the kingdom"—
this [verse] beginning with "To the three Rudras" is declared to be dedicated to Vāstoṣpati.
"By means of the 'dhruva' [mantra] offered with 'dhruveṇa', it shall bring about the attainment of a stable station;
likewise, O Rāma, the 'acyutā dyauḥ' [mantra] has been declared to grant the attainment of a station. (Vdho 2,127.24)
The mantra "payo deveṣu" (the milk among the gods), when offered as a sacrifice, is supreme for bestowing the increase of wealth;
the mantra "yunakrasīra" (you have yoked the plowshare) brings about the gain of agriculture through the dog.
"This is your womb"—this [mantra], when offered as a sacrifice, brings about the birth of a son;
likewise, "May the calves thrive"—this, when offered, causes the increase of cattle.
"...meti" is said to bring about preeminence in all things;
"ahaṃ te bhaga" is that which increases good fortune. Vdho_2,127.27 //
Those snares of yours—this [teaching] is nevertheless the means of liberation from such bonds;
and this [realization] that "it is not one's own" is the supreme destroyer of enemies.
"‘The slayer of rivals’—thus it is; there should be no hesitation in this regard.
‘Thou art the most excellent’—this is the supreme increaser of glory."
Just as the *mṛgo gopāyasi* hymn increases the good fortune of women,
so too has this *ā no agne* hymn been described as bestowing the attainment of a husband.
By means of this, one will indeed obtain food and it shall bring about the conception of a child;
likewise, by reciting "imaṃ tapasvin," it shall increase one's good fortune.

Whatever is offered upon the earth according to the prescribed rule, having performed the recitation (*śaṃsana*), it should be known as such; no doubt should be entertained in this matter. Vdho 2,127.32... // 127.32 //
"Śiva with the Śivās"—this [mantra] shall bring about the highest welfare.
This [mantra] "kṛtyādūṣaṇa" is called the "Kṛtyādūṣaṇa";
may Bṛhaspati protect one on the road, and there shall be a blessing for a safe journey.
May this mind indeed become a giver of fearlessness and a source of well-being on the path;
by the grace of Agni, may this Agni be our overseer.
He who should carry fire upon his head for a full year.
Facing the direction of Agni, one should constantly recite this mantra, which is the fire-invoking [mantra].
O Rāma, when a year has passed, one should perform the igniting of the fire.
One should mutter this unsurpassed mantra, "dūṣyā dūṣī," and perform the binding of the *pratisarā* cord, which destroys all defects.
The Prāṇasūkta has been declared, as well as that which increases vitality;
and "muñcāmi tvā" has been declared for liberation from untimely death.
One who studies the Atharvaśiras is liberated from all sins;
for it is the supreme purifier, the destroyer of all impurities.
Thus, O Rāma, these auspicious mantras have been recounted by me to you in brief, having extracted them from each Veda according to their primary importance.
O tiger among the Bhṛgus, thousands of applications for each individual mantra have been declared by the great-souled authors of the Purāṇas.
O fortunate one, it is not possible to describe them even in hundreds of years;
however, I have set forth for you some of the primary rites of these mantras.
Regarding the household where I have not previously specified the materials for you, I shall now describe the sacrificial offerings; listen as I speak of them.
The first oblation consists of sacrificial wood from trees fit for sacrifice,
as well as clarified butter, rice, and likewise white mustard seeds.
Unbroken grains, sesame seeds, curd, and milk, O Bhārgava,
as well as darbha grass, dūrvā grass, bilva fruits, and lotuses.
"O Bhārgava, knower of dharma, these substances— oil, fuel, rājikā, blood, and poison— are said to bring about pacification and nourishment;
one should employ thorny fuel-sticks in rites of malevolent magic."
O best of the Bhṛgus, one should not perform recitation or burnt offerings with a mantra without knowing its seer, its deity, and its meter. Vdho_2,127.47.
Whatever remains unmanifest in the Vedic hymns, the Brāhmaṇas, or the Sūktas,
one should determine that together with the learned and then bring it down into the sacrificial ritual.
Whatever the requisites, wherever they are, whatever the substances, and whatever the procedure for each specific branch— such is the established rule regarding their authority.
He who, transgressing his own sūtra, proceeds according to the sūtra of another,
having treated the Seer as an authority, is likewise joined with unrighteousness.

Therefore, with every effort, one should not transgress one's own Sūtra. O twice-born, in all rites that must be performed, both the earlier Tantra and the later Tantra are authoritative for one's own branch; the procedure for the rite is prescribed in between them.
O foremost descendant of Bhṛgu, this Ātharvaṇa ritual has been told to you in brief;
tell me, O one with long reddish eyes, what further shall I say to you beyond this?

Thus ends the one hundred and twenty-seventh chapter, titled "The Narration of the Atharva Ritual," within the account of Puṣkara told to Rāma, in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra, in the second section of the glorious Viṣṇudharmottara.
